# Tab Window Limiter

Chromium extension that caps normal browser windows and unpinned tabs. There is no website. The interface is the toolbar popup in `src/popup.html`.

## Behavior

- Default cap: 10 unpinned tabs in normal windows, and 1 normal window.
- Only the newly created tab or window is closed. Tabs already open, including ones opened during a pause, stay open.
- Pinned tabs, popup windows, and DevTools are not counted and are not closed.
- Incognito windows are closed as soon as they open. Chromium hides those windows from the extension until "Allow in Incognito" is enabled.
- Pause lasts 10 seconds, then enforcement turns back on. Resume turns it back on immediately.
- The toolbar badge is grey (`#808080`) and shows the count of every Chrome window.
- Saved state is a number in `chrome.storage.local` under the key `tabWindowLimiter`: the epoch milliseconds when the limiter was last paused. Missing or invalid values mean the limiter is on. Do not replace that number with a boolean.

## Popup controls

- Pause or resume: button id `tabWindowLimiter`, data-testid `limiter-toggle`. Visible label is "Pause limiter" or "Resume limiter".
- Status: id `status`, data-testid `limiter-status`, aria-live polite.
- Unpinned tabs: id `tabs`, data-testid `tab-count`.
- Normal windows: id `normal-windows`, data-testid `normal-window-count`.
- All windows (same number as the badge): id `windows`, data-testid `window-count`.
- What the limits mean: id `limits`.
- Errors: id `error`, role alert.

## Develop

- Load unpacked the `src` directory. There is no compile step. Reload the extension after edits.
- Change `MAX_TABS`, `MAX_WINDOWS`, `PAUSE_MS`, or `DISABLE_INCOGNITO` in `src/shared.js`.
- `npm test`, `npm run lint`, and `npm run build` need Node.js 22 and no installed packages.
